title: Death inquest scheduled for man shot dead by police outside Moose Jaw in 2022
article: A date has been set for the inquest into Ryan Booker's death. The 26-year-old was shot dead by police following a pursuit on Highway 1 near Moose Jaw in 2022.
The inquest will be held at the Royal Hotel in Regina, from June 23 to June 26.
In its announcement, the province noted that the purpose of a coroner's inquest is to establish who died, when and where it happened and the medical cause and manner of death.
The coroner's jury may make recommendations to prevent similar deaths in the future.
According to information provided by police at the time - the incident occurred in the early morning hours of July 17, 2022.
Just after 1 a.m., a man was spotted with a gun, reportedly uttering threats in a parking lot in Moose Jaw.
Police responded but the suspect fled the area leading to a pursuit on Highway 1 - which ended near Belle Plaine when the suspect pulled over.
Crisis negotiators attempted to de-escalate the situation to no avail. The situation escalated dramatically following a six-hour standoff.
At around 7 a.m., Booker pointed a gun at police and did not respond to commands from officers. He was shot and received medical attention soon after but died at the scene.
Immediately following the incident, the Moose Jaw Police Service and Saskatchewan RCMP requested that the Saskatoon Police Service conduct an independent investigation of the incident.
